name: National Industrial Recovery Act
kicker: 1933 New Deal recovery law · Created the NRA and its Blue Eagle
briefing: In June 1933, Franklin Roosevelt signed the National Industrial Recovery Act, hoping to end the Great Depression by having each industry agree on fair prices, wages, and working hours. Stores and factories that joined in hung up a Blue Eagle sign that said “We Do Our Part.” The law also protected workers’ right to form unions, but in 1935 the Supreme Court struck it down in a case about chickens.
answerHtml: National Industrial Recovery Act (or NIRA; prompt on National Recovery Administration or NRA, the agency it created)
reject: schechter poultry corp v united states

qb.tip: Search QBReader for this answer line (Middle School + Easy High School, power-marked) to see how real tossups clue it.

tossups.p: In the 1935 “hot oil” case, _Panama Refining Co. v. Ryan_, the Supreme Court struck down this law’s rules on oil shipments because Congress had given the president too much power. Months later, the Court threw out this law’s industry codes in the “sick chicken” case.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this 1933 New Deal law that created the National Recovery Administration.

tossups.p: Chief Justice Charles Evans Hughes wrote for a unanimous Court that this law’s Live Poultry Code could not be enforced against four brothers who sold chickens in Brooklyn, because their business was not interstate commerce. Hughes also ruled that this law gave the president too much lawmaking power.
tossups.r: That 1935 case was _Schechter_ [“SHEK-ter”] _Poultry Corp. v. United States_. For 10 points, name this New Deal law.

tossups.p: Lawyer Clarence Darrow led a review board that reported in 1934 that the business rules created under this law helped big companies and hurt small ones. Each industry wrote its own set of those rules, which could set prices, limit production, and fix wages and working hours.
tossups.r: Businesses that followed them displayed a Blue Eagle. For 10 points, name this 1933 law that created the NRA.

tossups.p: Hugh S. Johnson, a retired Army general nicknamed “Old Iron Pants” who had helped run the draft during World War I, led the agency created by this law and was named _Time_ magazine’s Man of the Year for 1933.
tossups.r: That agency was the National Recovery Administration. For 10 points, name this New Deal law later struck down by the Supreme Court.

tossups.p: Organizers for John L. Lewis’s United Mine Workers told coal miners that “the President wants you to join the union” after this law’s Section 7(a) promised workers the right to organize. Senator Robert Wagner led a National Labor Board set up to enforce that promise.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this 1933 law whose agency, the NRA, used a Blue Eagle as its symbol.

tossups.p: The second part of this law set aside 3.3 billion dollars for public works, and Interior Secretary Harold Ickes [“ICK-eez”] ran the agency that spent it on projects such as dams, bridges, and schools. That agency was the Public Works Administration.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this 1933 law whose first part created the National Recovery Administration.

tossups.p: On signing this law, Franklin Roosevelt said that history would probably record it as “the most important and far-reaching legislation ever enacted by the American Congress.” He signed it on June 16, 1933, the last day of his first Hundred Days.
tossups.r: Its agency’s symbol was a Blue Eagle. For 10 points, name this law later struck down in the “sick chicken” case.

tossups.p: The first industry code approved under this law, for cotton textiles, banned mills from hiring children under 16. Hundreds of other industries, from steel to lumber, later wrote their own “codes of fair competition” under this law.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this 1933 law that created the National Recovery Administration and its Blue Eagle.

tossups.p: In July 1933, while industries were still writing codes under this law, employers were asked to sign a “blanket code” called the President’s Reemployment Agreement, promising higher wages and shorter workweeks for their employees.
tossups.r: Those who signed could display a Blue Eagle that said “We Do Our Part.” For 10 points, name this law that created the NRA.

tossups.p: On May 27, 1935, a day New Dealers called “Black Monday,” the Supreme Court ruled against Franklin Roosevelt in three cases, including one that struck down the industry codes created by this law. The Court said Congress could not hand the president the power to write such codes.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this 1933 law that created the National Recovery Administration and the Public Works Administration.

tossups.p: This law suspended the antitrust laws so that competing companies could agree on prices and output, while its Section 7(a) let workers bargain through unions of their own choosing. Each industry’s rules under this law were called a code of fair competition.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this New Deal law that created the NRA in 1933 and was struck down two years later.

tossups.p: After the Supreme Court struck down this law, Congress passed the Wagner Act in 1935 to restore its promise that workers could form unions. The Fair Labor Standards Act of 1938 later brought back its idea of a national minimum wage and maximum workweek.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this 1933 law whose National Recovery Administration used a Blue Eagle symbol.

tossups.p: This law’s system of industry codes was set to expire after two years, but less than three weeks before that deadline, the Supreme Court struck it down unanimously. Franklin Roosevelt complained that the ruling took the nation back to a “horse-and-buggy” definition of interstate commerce.
tossups.r: The case was nicknamed the “sick chicken” case. For 10 points, name this 1933 law that created the National Recovery Administration.

tossups.p: Justice Benjamin Cardozo [“kar-DOH-zoh”] called the power this law gave the president “delegation running riot” in a separate opinion agreeing with a 9–0 ruling against it. That ruling came in a case about a poultry business in Brooklyn.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this New Deal law that created the National Recovery Administration and was struck down in 1935.

tossups.p: This law tried to do for factories what the Agricultural Adjustment Act did for farms, letting producers limit output so that prices would rise. Both laws passed during the Hundred Days of 1933, and the Supreme Court struck down both of them, in 1935 and 1936.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this law whose National Recovery Administration used the Blue Eagle symbol.

trap.title: Law or agency?
trap.body: The National Industrial Recovery Act (NIRA) was the 1933 law. The National Recovery Administration (NRA), with its Blue Eagle, was the agency that law created, and the Public Works Administration was its other agency. Answering “NRA” to a question about the law earns only a prompt. The Wagner Act (1935) and the Works Progress Administration (WPA, 1935) are different New Deal answers.
trap.fix: Listen for the noun: “this law” or “this act” wants the National Industrial Recovery Act, and “this agency” wants the NRA. If you are prompted after saying “NRA,” give the full name of the act. In these questions, NRA never means the National Rifle Association.
trap.line: Real answer line: National Industrial Recovery Act (or NIRA; prompt on National Recovery Administration or NRA)
